title: 1986 AMC 8 Problem 18
statement: A rectangular grazing area is to be fenced off on three sides using part of a \(100\) meter rock wall as the fourth side. Fence posts are to be placed every \(12\) meters along the fence, including the two posts where the fence meets the rock wall. What is the fewest number of posts required to fence an area \(36\) m by \(60\) m?

solutions.text:
The fewest posts are used when the wall serves as the longer \(60\) meter side, so the fence covers two \(36\) meter sides and one \(60\) meter side, a path of \(36 + 60 + 36 = 132\) meters.

Placing a post every \(12\) meters, including both ends, uses \(\dfrac{132}{12} + 1 = 12\) posts.

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: To use the fewest posts, let the \(60\) meter side lie along the wall, so the fenced length is as short as possible
The fenced path is \(36 + 60 + 36 = 132\) meters; place a post every \(12\) meters, counting both ends
